skill.name: autonomous-agent-patterns
skill.description: Provides Python design patterns for autonomous coding agents, including tool calls, permissions, browser automation, context management, checkpoints, and MCP integration.
skill.summary: Design autonomous coding agents with practical architecture, tool, safety, browser, context, and MCP patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most external-command detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, and the hardcoded URLs are documentation references. Confirmed risks remain in copyable examples for shell execution, environment inheritance, arbitrary URL retrieval, filesystem access, prompt injection, screenshot disclosure, and unreviewed generated code.

remediation.issue: The sandbox example uses shell execution and passes the complete host environment.
remediation.suggestion: Use argument arrays with shell disabled, validate every argument, and provide a minimal environment allowlist.

remediation.issue: File tools accept unrestricted paths, and the workspace containment check uses a vulnerable string prefix test.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths canonically and require Path.relative_to against the workspace before every read, write, or directory operation.

remediation.issue: Caller-provided URLs and retrieved content are accepted without network or prompt-safety controls.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist schemes and hosts, block private addresses, set limits and timeouts, and label retrieved text as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Model-generated MCP server code is saved and connected without review or isolation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, static validation, dependency controls, and sandboxed execution before loading generated server code.

remediation.issue: Screenshots are sent to a model without redaction or a disclosure gate.
remediation.suggestion: Obtain user approval, restrict capture scope, redact sensitive regions, and document the destination and retention policy.

remediation.issue: Session approvals are cached only by tool name and can authorize later calls with different arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Bind approvals to normalized arguments, target resources, operation scope, and expiration.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Context Is Inserted Into Model Prompts
semantic_findings.description: File and URL content is inserted into the model context without trust labels or instruction isolation. Malicious content can attempt indirect prompt injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example reads arbitrary file and web content and concatenates it directly into the formatted prompt. No sanitization or instruction boundary is implemented.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Approved Reads Can Access Files Outside the Workspace
semantic_findings.description: The read tool accepts absolute paths, while the permission configuration automatically approves reads. This combination can expose local secrets to an autonomous agent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The schema explicitly requests an absolute path, execute opens it directly, and read_file is configured for automatic approval.

semantic_findings.title: Workspace Containment Uses an Unsafe Prefix Check
semantic_findings.description: The sandbox accepts any canonical path whose text starts with the workspace path. A sibling path with the same prefix can bypass containment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: String startswith does not enforce a path-component boundary, so a workspace such as /work/app also matches /work/application.

semantic_findings.title: Checkpoint Capture Interpolates a Path Into Shell Commands
semantic_findings.description: The workspace value is inserted into two shell command strings without quoting. Crafted paths can add shell operators and execute additional commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both subprocess.getoutput calls use f-strings containing workspace directly before shell operators. No validation or shell quoting is present.

semantic_findings.title: Generated MCP Code Is Loaded Without Review
semantic_findings.description: The agent writes model-generated Python and immediately connects it as an MCP server. Untrusted generated code can execute with the host process permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented flow generates code, writes it to server.py, and hot-loads the resulting server without approval, validation, or sandboxing.

semantic_findings.title: Screenshots Are Sent to a Model Without Redaction
semantic_findings.description: The visual agent sends full screenshots to the configured model. Pages can contain credentials, personal data, or private application content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both methods capture the current page and place the image data into an LLM chat request. No consent or redaction step appears.

semantic_findings.title: Session Approval Is Not Bound to Tool Arguments
semantic_findings.description: Approval is cached only by tool name. One approved edit or write can authorize later calls against different paths or content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The session_approvals dictionary is keyed only by tool_name and returns before evaluating the current args.

content.value_statement: Autonomous coding agents need reliable loops, tool contracts, permissions, and context handling. This skill provides Python patterns for architecture, browser automation, checkpoints, and MCP integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains iterative agent loops that plan, call tools, observe results, and stop after a configured limit.
Defines Python tool schemas and examples for reading, editing, searching, commanding, browsing, and requesting user input.
Shows permission levels, approval caching, command allowlists, and workspace validation concepts.
Demonstrates browser navigation, screenshots, accessible text extraction, and vision-guided interaction.
Presents context collection, checkpoint persistence, multi-model routing, and MCP tool discovery patterns.
limitations: The examples are reference patterns and are not a complete runnable framework.
Several examples require stronger path, shell, network, prompt, and privacy controls before production use.
The model names and library interfaces may require updates for the selected provider.
The skill does not provide deployment, monitoring, authentication, or comprehensive automated tests.

use_cases.title: Prototype an Agent Loop
use_cases.description: Create a bounded loop that selects tools, records observations, and returns a final response.

use_cases.title: Design Tool Approval Rules
use_cases.description: Classify agent operations by risk and define when each action needs user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Plan an MCP Extension
use_cases.description: Outline tool discovery, server registration, context handling, and review gates for an MCP integration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a bounded agent loop for [task]. List its states, stopping conditions, available tools, and error handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when starting a small autonomous agent.

prompt_templates.title: Define Tool Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create tool contracts for [workflow]. Include parameters, validation, results, failures, and permission levels for each tool.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when an agent needs reliable tool interfaces.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agent Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent design: [design]. Identify path, command, network, privacy, approval, and prompt-injection risks. Propose specific controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before implementing tools with side effects.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Agent Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production architecture for [system]. Cover model routing, tools, approvals, sandboxing, browser controls, context isolation, checkpoints, MCP, observability, and recovery.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for an advanced system design review.

output_examples.input: Design a small coding agent that can inspect a repository and suggest changes.
output: Loop: inspect, plan, request tools, observe, summarize.
Automatic actions: list files and search code inside the workspace.
Approved actions: read sensitive files, edit files, and run commands.
Stop after ten iterations or when no tool call is needed.

output_examples.input: Create permission rules for a browser testing agent.
output: Allow navigation only to approved test domains.
Require approval before form submission, download, upload, or screenshot sharing.
Block credential pages and private network addresses.
Record each approved action with its target and arguments.

output_examples.input: Outline a safe MCP tool creation workflow.
output_examples.output: Generate the server in an isolated workspace, validate its dependencies, review its permissions, run tests, request approval, then register it.

best_practices: Set iteration, time, token, and cost limits before starting autonomous work.
Validate paths, arguments, URLs, and model outputs at every tool boundary.
Require scoped approval and audit logging for actions with external side effects.
anti_patterns: Do not pass model-generated text directly to a shell, browser action, or code loader.
Do not treat retrieved files, web pages, or tool results as trusted instructions.
Do not cache broad approvals without binding them to targets, arguments, and expiration.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a runnable agent framework?
faq.answer: No. It provides Python reference patterns that require integration, dependency setup, validation, and testing.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does the skill cover human approval?
faq.answer: Yes. It presents automatic, session, per-action, and denied permission levels with an approval manager example.

faq.question: Can the browser patterns handle visual pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples capture screenshots and use a vision model, but production systems need consent and redaction controls.

faq.question: Does it include MCP integration?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows server connection, tool discovery, and generated server registration as conceptual patterns.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. Strengthen shell isolation, path containment, network validation, prompt boundaries, privacy controls, approvals, and test coverage first.
